prompt:
One standalone finished illustration for Tomorrow and Tomorrow, a civilization strategy game. Wide 3:2 landscape composition. The named discovery and its distinctive action or mechanism must read in a central banner crop. Depict the stated historical stage with only materials, dress, tools, buildings, and infrastructure available then. The scene belongs to an alternative-history world: no recognizable real landmark, historical person, nation, flag, or emblem. Vary setting, distance, viewpoint, age, and gender across the batch. No legible text, letters, numbers, captions, logo, watermark, border, UI, montage, voxel geometry, cartoon, photography, or CGI. Any marks on records, signs, and screens are illegible. The field's medium is the way the illustration is rendered, never an object or technology that must appear inside the scene.
Research direction: Craft & industry.
Medium and finish: Tactile impasto oil painting with visible bold strokes and strong material texture.
Palette: Burnished copper, ember orange, soot black, dark umber.
Composition: Show the transformation of material and the specific apparatus or process; use the real source of heat or light when present.
Historical span: Information age; specific date: 2829 (~AD 1960).
Specific discovery, Industrial Robots: A hydraulic arm swings a spot-welding gun from seam to seam on the car body, tirelessly repeating the motions taught to it on the first day. Paint it as a late twentieth to early twenty-first century scene.
review: Visual pilot reviewed at central card crop on 2026-09-25; confirm historical details when later research block integrates.
